constitutive_assumptions: In analytical modeling, deformation is based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with axial strain approximated as a superposition of a linearly varying vertical field and a constant vertical field, with an interfacial displacement variable.
Interfacial interactions are modeled using Coulomb friction with a penalty friction formulation.
In finite element modeling of jamming structures, layers are treated as homogeneous 2D plane-strain linear elastic bodies with large-deformation analysis enabled.

In variable kinematics finite element simulations, unjammed jamming structures are approximated by scaling down the elastic modulus by a factor of n^2 (n = 20), and cable loading is approximated as a pure bending moment.
control_variables: Layer material (HP Ultra White Multipurpose Copy Paper)
Envelope material and sealing process (thermoplastic polyurethane sheet, heat pressed at 100 °C, tube sealed at 171 °C)
Loading anvil displacement rate in three-point bending (25 mm min^-1)
Actuator and substrate elastomeric materials (Dragon Skin 10 Medium silicone, Sylgard 184 PDMS, and Ecoflex 00-10 silicone)
dependent_variables: Bending stiffness across pre-slip, transition, and full-slip regimes
Slip propagation length along layer interfaces
Critical transition loads (first and second transition loads)
Discreteness of bending quantified by the ratio of maximum to mean curvature (kappa_max / kappa_mean)
Multiaxis stiffness (in-plane bending, off-axis bending, and torsional stiffness)
Perturbation resistance / dislodging force in robotic grasping

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Laminar jamming structures subjected to a pressure gradient transition through three distinct mechanical regimes under load: pre-slip (cohesive layers, maximum stiffness scaling as n^2, zero damping), transition regime (progressive interfacial slip, declining stiffness, frictional damping), and full-slip (complete interfacial slip, minimal stiffness, maximal damping).
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: analytical modeling, finite element simulation, and experimental observation

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Two-dimensional plane-strain finite element models predict three-point bending force-deflection behavior of many-layer jamming structures with high accuracy across varying layer counts and vacuum pressures without fitting parameters, achieving a minimum coefficient of determination (R^2) of 0.9879.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: finite element simulation and experimental validation

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Integrating a 20-layer paper laminar jamming structure with a pneumatic soft bending actuator enables shape-locking, maintaining the actuated curved configuration upon depressurization with high geometric fidelity (R^2 = 0.9835) when an 85 kPa vacuum is applied.

A composite structure comprising an elastic substrate and a segmented laminar jamming structure demonstrates variable kinematics, transitioning from continuous bending (vacuum off) to discrete jointed bending (vacuum on) with a 6.65-fold increase in the ratio of maximum to mean curvature.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: finite element simulation and experimental demonstration

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A two-fingered grasper using variable kinematics fingers can perform wrap grasps on large objects (20 cm diameter) when unjammed and stable pinch grasps on small objects (one-eighth the diameter) when jammed, exhibiting a 32-fold increase in primary bending stiffness, a 2.5-fold increase in off-axis bending stiffness, a 2.7-fold increase in torsional stiffness, and an 8-fold increase in perturbation resistance.

Analytical and finite element modeling reveals that full-slip damping force scales linearly with the number of layers, the vacuum pressure, and the coefficient of friction (succinctly mu*P*b*h for a two-layer structure).
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: analytical derivation and finite element scaling analysis

experimental_setup: HP Ultra White Multipurpose Copy Paper strips cut via laser cutter and enclosed within vacuum-formed thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) envelopes heat-pressed at 100 °C with TPU tubing sealed at 171 °C.
Instron 5566 universal testing machine configured with a three-point bending fixture operated at a crosshead displacement rate of 25 mm min^-1.
Cole-Parmer manual vacuum regulator (EW-07061-30) for setting vacuum pressure levels.
Pneumatic soft bending actuator molded from Dragon Skin 10 Medium platinum-cure silicone rubber bonded to jamming structures using Dow Corning 795 silicone building sealant.
Variable kinematics substrate cast from Sylgard 184 PDMS with an internal channel for a braided polyethylene cable (Hollow Spectra) tensioned via a turnbuckle.
Fingertips for a two-fingered grasper cast from Ecoflex 00-10 silicone rubber.
Chatillon DFI10 digital force gauge with custom fixtures for multiaxis stiffness and grasp perturbation measurements.
future_work: Approximating high-layer-count jamming structures as a single crystal with a single slip system to reduce finite element computational runtime.
Incorporating a one-way valve to maintain vacuum without requiring a tethered continuous vacuum source.
Using electrostatic actuation or elastic actuation (such as external elastic mesh envelopes or spring clips) to overcome ambient atmospheric pressure limits on normal force.
Applying variable kinematics to medical and surgical devices traversing vasculature before applying high forces, as well as continuum manipulators.
independent_variables: Number of layers (e.g., 5, 10, 15, 20 layers; n=2 for analytical model)
Vacuum pressure (e.g., 0 kPa, 24 kPa, 47 kPa, 71 kPa, 85 kPa)
Coefficient of friction between layers (simulated at 0.25, 0.50, 0.65, 0.75)
Applied transverse load and deflection during bending
Actuation state (vacuum on vs. vacuum off; pneumatic inflation pressure at 16 kPa; cable tension)
limitations_inferred: Testing was conducted quasi-statically at a low displacement rate (25 mm min^-1), leaving dynamic response, high-rate impact behavior, fatigue, wear, and viscoelastic relaxation over extended cycling uncharacterized.
Cellulose paper layers and TPU envelopes may be susceptible to degradation, moisture absorption, and puncture failure in wet or rough operational environments.

Finite element and analytical formulations assume 2D plane-strain behavior, neglecting 3D edge effects, out-of-plane anticlastic curvature, and torsional-bending coupling in the jamming laminate itself.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Finite element simulation execution time scales linearly with the number of layers, becoming computationally prohibitive for structures with exceptionally high layer counts.
The physical shape-locking prototype required a vacuum source to remain connected after actuator depressurization, complicating operation without external support equipment.
Vacuum actuation restricts the maximum pressure gradient to ambient atmospheric pressure, which caps the maximum load sustainable before the structure slips and softens.
As the number of layers increases, achieving a homogeneous vacuum pressure distribution throughout the structure may become physically challenging.
The coefficient of friction could not be precisely adjusted experimentally, preventing direct experimental validation of varying friction.
main_results: Formulated an analytical model extending Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with interfacial friction and slip, capturing all three deformation regimes (pre-slip, transition, full-slip), slip propagation, and transition loads in two-layer jamming beams.

Constructed 2D plane-strain finite element models accurately capturing the mechanical response of many-layer jamming structures without fitting parameters, matching three-point bending data with R^2 >= 0.9879.
Extracted scaling relations showing full-slip damping scales linearly with layer count, vacuum pressure, and friction coefficient.
Achieved shape-locking in a pneumatic soft actuator, preserving its curved pressurized configuration upon depressurization with R^2 = 0.9835 when 85 kPa vacuum was applied.
Demonstrated variable kinematics in a hybrid cable-actuated beam, switching from continuous bending to discrete jointed bending with a 6.65x increase in peak-to-mean curvature ratio.

Fabricated a two-fingered grasper executing wrap grasps on a 20 cm ball and pinch grasps on a 2.5 cm ball, with jammed fingers providing >32x bending stiffness, 2.5x off-axis stiffness, 2.7x torsional stiffness, and >8x perturbation dislodging resistance.
modeling_methods: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory extended for vacuum pressure, interfacial friction, and interfacial slip
Boundary-value problem formulation and explicit analytical solution for cantilevered two-layer jamming beams under uniform distributed load
Two-dimensional plane-strain finite element analysis (ABAQUS 6.14r2) with penalty contact friction formulation and large-deformation analysis
performance_metrics: Bending stiffness (pre-slip, transition, and full-slip stiffness values; n^2 theoretical multiplier; >=32-fold measured increase in finger bending stiffness)
Goodness-of-fit coefficient of determination (R^2 >= 0.9879 for FEA vs. experimental bending force; R^2 = 0.9835 for shape-locking fidelity)
Discreteness ratio (maximum curvature to mean curvature, kappa_max / kappa_mean, increasing by a factor of 6.65)
Perturbation resistance force (at least 8-fold increase in dislodging force for pinch grasping)
Off-axis bending stiffness (2.5-fold increase under vacuum)
Full-slip damping force (analytically expressed as mu*P*b*h)
Experimental repeatability (maximum deviation of 0.24 N across loading cycles and samples)
possible_gap_implications: The validated analytical and finite element frameworks allow predictable, model-based design of variable-stiffness laminar jamming components without relying solely on iterative physical prototyping.

Variable kinematics demonstrates that soft robots can programmatically switch between continuous continuum deformation and discrete jointed kinematics, which may simplify sensing, state estimation, and control algorithms by leveraging multi-rigid-body dynamics.
Extending laminar jamming models from planar 2D bending to spatial 3D bending and coupled torsional deformations remains an opportunity for future continuum manipulator design.
paper.research_objective: To develop and experimentally validate comprehensive analytical and finite element models of laminar jamming across all deformation regimes, and to integrate jamming structures into soft machines to achieve shape-locking and variable kinematics (enabling reversible transitions between continuous soft deformation and discrete jointed rigid behavior).
paper.research_problem: Bridging the divide between compliant soft machines and high-force, precise rigid robots. Existing variable-stiffness technologies suffer from limited range/resolution per unit weight, slow transition speeds, poor bending resistance, and inability to transition between continuous and discrete jointed deformations. Furthermore, prior laminar jamming research lacked predictive models beyond pre-slip, hindering practical design and kinematic adaptation.
paper.robot_type: soft machines, pneumatic soft bending actuator, cable-actuated variable kinematics system, two-fingered grasper, continuum manipulators
paper.title: Mechanically Versatile Soft Machines through Laminar Jamming
